title: Cuentos de la selva
author: Horacio Quiroga
blurb: Eight animal stories from the forest of Misiones, written for children: a turtle, flamingos, a parrot and a war of alligators.
note: Published in 1918, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Henri Rousseau, Surprised! (Tiger in a Tropical Storm), 1891. National Gallery, London. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Platero y yo
author: Juan Ramón Jiménez
blurb: Short, gentle chapters about a poet and his small donkey in an Andalusian village.
note: The first edition came out in 1914, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931). The old spelling of the preposition a (written á) is modernized.
coverCredit: Modesto Teixidor, Women Riding a Donkey, about 1890. Museo Art Nouveau y Art Déco Casa Lis, Salamanca. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Cuentos de amor, de locura y de muerte (selección)
author: Horacio Quiroga
blurb: Four dark stories: a snakebite in the jungle, a feather pillow, a hen, and a sunstroke.
note: Published in 1917, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Henri Rousseau, The Snake Charmer, 1907. Musée d’Orsay, Paris. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Leyendas (selección)
author: Gustavo Adolfo Bécquer
blurb: Three legends of Spain: green eyes in a spring, the haunted hill of souls, and a ray of moonlight.
note: Written in the 1860s, the author died in 1870. The old spelling of the preposition a (written á) is modernized.
coverCredit: Valeriano Bécquer, Portrait of Gustavo Adolfo Bécquer, his brother, 1862. Museo de Bellas Artes de Sevilla. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: El sombrero de tres picos
author: Pedro Antonio de Alarcón
blurb: A miller, his clever wife, and a lecherous magistrate in a comic night of mistaken identities.
note: Published in 1874 and the author died in 1891, so it is in the US public domain.
coverCredit: Francisco de Goya, The Parasol (El quitasol), 1777. Museo del Prado, Madrid. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: La vida de Lazarillo de Tormes
author: Anónimo
blurb: A poor boy serves a string of masters, from a blind beggar to a priest, and learns to live by his wits.
note: Published in 1554 by an unknown author, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, The Young Beggar, about 1645–50. Musée du Louvre, Paris. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Marianela
author: Benito Pérez Galdós
blurb: A girl who has always led a blind young man around a mining village fears what will happen when he can see.
note: Published in 1878 and the author died in 1920, so it is in the US public domain.
coverCredit: Francisco de Goya, The Blind Guitarist (El ciego de la guitarra), 1778. Museo del Prado, Madrid. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
